questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A consumer seeks to maximise his utility. Up to what point should he continue to consume each good?

options.A: until the marginal utility per dollar from each good is the same
options.B: until the marginal utility from each good is the same
options.C: until the marginal utility from each good reaches a maximum
options.D: until the marginal utility from each good is zero

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for labour. money wage rate D O number employed What could cause the demand curve to shift to the right?

options.A: a decrease in labour productivity
options.C: an increase in the average price level
options.D: a fall in the money wage rate

questions.questionText: A firm currently employs 100 workers at a daily wage rate of $500 per worker. It calculates that the marginal cost per day of hiring an additional worker would be $702. By how much would the daily wage rate per worker have to be increased to attract an extra worker?
A trade union seeks to increase the wages that a firm pays to its workers while at the same time avoiding any job losses. What will weaken the union’s negotiating position?

options.A: Capital and labour are close substitutes.
options.B: The firm enjoys monopsony power in a labour market.
options.C: The demand for the good produced by the firm is price-inelastic.
options.D: The supply of labour to the firm is highly inelastic.

questions.questionText: A firm employs two factors of production, capital and labour. The curves in the diagram show the different combinations of capital and labour a firm needs to produce given levels of output. capital Q = 300 units Q = 200 units Q = 100 units O labour What does the diagram show?

options.A: the firm’s long-run production function
options.B: the firm’s long-run total cost function
options.C: the firm’s short-run production function
options.D: the firm’s short-run total cost function

questions.questionText: What will be the effect on price and output of a subsidy on each item produced by a profit maximising monopolist? effect on price effect on output

options.A: decrease increase
options.C: unchanged increase

options.A: Curve 1 is the marginal cost curve.
options.B: Curve 2 is the average variable cost curve.
options.C: Curve 3 is the average fixed cost curve.
options.D: Curve 4 is the average total cost curve.

What determines the contestability of a market?

options.A: the costs of entry and exit
options.B: the degree of differentiation of the product
options.C: the number of firms in the industry
options.D: the price elasticity of demand for the product

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the change in an industry’s cost of production when it moves from perfect competition to monopoly. There is no change in the demand for the industry’s product. MC (perfect competition) price MC (monopoly) D MR O output What effect will the change in market structure in this industry have on price, output and consumer surplus? consumer price output surplus

options.A: increase increase reduce
options.C: reduce increase increase

questions.questionText: A firm decides to maximise sales revenue rather than profits. What is likely to be one of the consequences of this decision?

options.A: an increase in the price of the firm’s product
options.B: a reduction in the price of the firm’s shares
options.C: a reduction in the firm’s market share
options.D: a reduction in the number employed by the firm

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a profit-maximising monopolist. MC x AC costs, y revenue z w AR MR O output Which area measures the deadweight loss arising from the exercise of monopoly power?

options.A: x + y B y C y + z D w + z

questions.questionText: Income inequality can be measured by the Gini coefficient. On a scale of 0 to 100, the higher the value the greater the inequality. The table below shows three Gini coefficient values for four OECD countries. The first is from wages, the second when government welfare payments are included and the third when welfare payments and government health and education spending are included. In which country did welfare payments make the greatest contribution to income redistribution? inequality after inequality after wages, welfare inequality after wages and welfare payments and wages from work payments health and education spending
What is an advantage of means-tested benefits over universal benefits?

options.A: an increase in the percentage of those who take up benefits for which they are eligible
options.B: a reduction in the rate at which benefits are withdrawn as households’ incomes increase
options.C: a reduction in the poverty trap
options.D: the targeting of benefits on those in greatest need
